vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not escalate or switch antidepressants on the assumption of treatment-resistant depression before the vascular diagnosis is considered
Do not prescribe anticholinergic or sedating agents (first-generation antihistamines, tricyclics, benzodiazepines) in a patient with small-vessel disease and falls risk
Do not start an antipsychotic for apathy
Do not accept 'she is just depressed' as the endpoint of the assessment when instrumental independence has been lost
required_recommendations: Distinguish apathy from depression formally rather than assuming the antidepressant failed for want of dose
Document the cognitive deficit on a validated instrument and record cue-responsiveness of recall
Exclude the reversible causes of cognitive impairment with the named screen
Obtain brain MRI with SWI and grade the small-vessel burden in STRIVE-2 terms
Confirm the deficit is genuine with performance-validity measures where a psychiatric attribution has already been made
Address smoking, blood pressure, lipids and CPAP adherence — the only interventions that alter the course
Assess home safety, including the gas ring and medication management

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

accepted: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type, with frontal-subcortical apathy previously misattributed to depression

differential.key_features: Apathy without sadness, a Geriatric Depression Scale of 4/15, an Apathy Evaluation Scale of 48, no response to eight months of therapeutic sertraline, and passed performance-validity measures place this below the vascular explanation
Recall is fully cue-responsive, the medial temporal lobes are preserved, and the deficit is dominated by slowing rather than forgetting
Poor CPAP adherence with an Epworth of 13 is a genuine contributor worth correcting, but it does not explain a Fazekas 3 white matter burden or the loss of instrumental independence
Apathy is prominent but there is no disinhibition, no loss of empathy, no compulsivity, no dietary change and no frontotemporal atrophy
Evans index 0.26 with no ventriculomegaly and no magnetic gait

key_clinical_evidence: Apathy and depression are dissociable and the distinction is measurable: an elevated Apathy Evaluation Scale with a low Geriatric Depression Scale and no response to an adequate antidepressant trial points to frontal-subcortical disease

An insidious rather than stepwise course does not argue against small-vessel disease — progressive confluent white matter change produces gradual decline, and only the multi-infarct mechanism is characteristically stepwise
Performance-validity measures matter once a psychiatric attribution has been made, because they are what distinguish a genuine deficit from an effort-dependent one
Smoking and untreated hypertension are the two drivers here and both are modifiable; no additional imaging changes management
Poor CPAP adherence is a real contributor to cognitive impairment and should be corrected, but it cannot be the whole explanation in the presence of a Fazekas 3 burden

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: An adequately dosed antidepressant trial that produced no change in eight months, with apathy dissociated from low mood on formal scales, argues against depression as the explanation

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 20/30 with executive dysfunction, marked psychomotor slowing and fully cue-responsive recall. The Apathy Evaluation Scale is clinically elevated at 48 while the Geriatric Depression Scale is 4/15, and eight months of sertraline at a therapeutic dose produced no change: this is the frontal-subcortical apathy of small-vessel disease, not a depressive episode.

labs.interpretation: LDL 142 mg/dL is well above target for a patient with established cerebrovascular disease. HbA1c 5.9% indicates impaired glucose regulation without diabetes. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative. There is no anaemia and renal function is preserved.

mri.impression: Severe sporadic small-vessel disease with confluent frontal-predominant white matter hyperintensity (Fazekas 3), three chronic lacunes and moderately enlarged perivascular spaces. No microbleeds, no cortical infarcts, medial temporal lobes preserved. The burden accounts for the frontal-subcortical syndrome.

specialized_test.impression: Executive dysfunction and slowed processing with intact recognition memory, and performance-validity measures passed — the deficit is genuine and not effort-dependent, which is the distinction that matters when depression has been assumed.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Severe unambiguous small-vessel burden; the difficulty lies only in overriding an existing psychiatric label, and the formal scales resolve it
key_educational_points: Frontal-subcortical apathy in small-vessel disease is routinely misdiagnosed as depression; the scales dissociate them
A gradual course is compatible with small-vessel vascular dementia — stepwise decline is a feature of the multi-infarct mechanism, not of every vascular dementia
Performance-validity measures belong in the battery whenever a psychiatric explanation has already been applied
Smoking cessation and blood-pressure control are the treatment; there is no disease-modifying drug

patient.chief_complaint: Eighteen months of slowing, apathy and forgetfulness that her daughter says is not depression

family_history: Mother had a stroke at 74 and died at 79

social_history.living_situation: Lives alone since her husband died 3 years ago; a daughter visits daily

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Renata Bosco is a 71-year-old retired ward clerk who attends with her daughter for evaluation of 18 months of cognitive decline. The daughter's account is that her mother 'stopped starting things'. She used to cook every day and telephone her grandchildren; now she sits in the same chair for most of the afternoon, the fridge holds expired food, and she has to be prompted to shower. She is not sad, does not cry, denies hopelessness and sleeps rather too much than too little. Her general practitioner started sertraline eight months ago on the assumption of a depressive episode; there has been no change in eight months at a therapeutic dose. Cognitively the daughter reports slowness rather than forgetting: her mother eventually recalls conversations and appointments, particularly when reminded of the context, but cannot follow a recipe with several steps, has twice left the gas ring on, and now takes an hour to do what used to take fifteen minutes. She has stopped managing her own bank card. There have been no discrete episodes of weakness or speech difficulty, no falls, no visual hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. She continues to smoke fifteen cigarettes a day, and her blood pressure has been between 150 and 170 systolic at every recorded visit for the past two years. She uses her CPAP machine perhaps two nights a week.

neurological_exam.additional: No resting tremor, no rigidity at the wrists. Glabellar tap unsuppressed. Nocturia three times nightly. Epworth Sleepiness Scale 13/24 with inconsistent CPAP use.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin. No dysmetria.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Visual fields full to confrontation. Mild bilateral hypomimia. Speech mildly dysarthric with imprecise consonants. Palate symmetric, tongue midline.
neurological_exam.gait: Cautious, short-stepped, mildly wide-based with preserved arm swing. Turns en bloc in four steps. Tandem impossible. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, gives the year correctly but the month as two months earlier. MoCA 20/30, losing points on trail-making, digit span backwards, serial sevens, verbal fluency (9 animals) and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 with cues). Marked psychomotor slowing. Affect flat rather than sad; she denies sadness and says she simply cannot be bothered.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Tone mildly increased in both legs. Strength 5/5 throughout. No drift, no tremor.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ at the knees, 2+ elsewhere. Plantar responses flexor. Palmomental reflex present.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration and proprioception throughout.
